title: Both handlers fall back to CloudPostureScan.findById(scanId) with NO organizationId filter when the org-scoped lookup misses, unlike the sibling getScanProgress (line 215) which re-checks scan.organizationId === req.orgId after the identical fallback and throws 403 if not.
description: Route middleware's getScanProjectId (scan.routes.js) is itself org-scoped, so for a foreign-org scanId it returns null; because the route uses requireProjectMembership({...,required:false}), a null result lets the request through instead of blocking it. The unscoped findById fallback then returns the OTHER organization's full scan + findings (or generates a PDF/CSV/Excel export of it). Any authenticated user who learns/guesses another org's scan _id can read or export that org's complete cloud security findings. CONFIRMED by direct code read of all 3 functions + the route middleware chain.
affectedFiles: vibrantix-backend/src/modules/cloud-posture/scan.routes.js:157-171 (results route), :180-194 (export route) — now also gated by requireProjectMembership
tags: verified-note: Yes - full exploit chain traced and confirmed
fixEvidence: Re-read getScanResults (scan.controller.js:395-430) and exportScanResults (:436-461) in full. Both now build the fallback ObjectId lookup as `CloudPostureScan.findOne({ _id: scanId, ...buildOrgFilter(req) })` — i.e. the fallback carries the SAME organizationId filter as the primary scanId lookup; there is no bare findById anywhere in either handler. A foreign-org scan/ObjectId now resolves to `scan === null` on both the primary and fallback query, and the handler throws AppError.notFound('Scan not found') before any data is read. Additionally, scan.routes.js's PLAC Phase 0/2 fix now adds requireProjectMembership({ getProjectId: getScanProjectId, required: false }) plus augmentPermissionsWithProjectGrant to both the /results/:scanId and /:scanId/export routes (routes.js:157-171, 180-194), so the route-level gate has also been hardened on top of the controller-level org fix. The described exploit chain no longer reproduces.

title: getScanProgress unconditionally overrides the MongoDB status with the Redis cache's status (status = cacheData.status || dbStatus) with no timestamp/staleness comparison against dbStatus. The Python worker's redis_cache.delete_scan_status() is defined but never called anywhere, so the stale key only expires after a fixed 1-hour TTL.
description: If a Prowler worker crashes mid-scan after writing status:'running' to Redis, scan-reconciler.job.js correctly marks Mongo status:'abandoned' within minutes, but getScanProgress keeps returning the stale cached 'running X%' for up to the remaining hour - the user sees an apparently-live scan that will never move again. CONFIRMED: verified the unconditional override at the exact lines cited.
affectedFiles: vibrantix-prowler/src/utils/redis_cache.py:143-156 (delete_scan_status defined) — grep-confirmed 2026-08-24: zero call sites anywhere in vibrantix-prowler/src
tags: verified-note: Yes - unconditional cache override confirmed at the exact lines cited

title: None of the frontend's 3 'is this scan done?' terminal-status checks (nor the backend's own progress-percentage switch) include 'abandoned', 'timed_out', or 'completed_with_warnings' - all 3 are real, live terminal statuses (abandoned is set in 5 places by scan-reconciler.job.js; completed_with_warnings/timed_out are real model enum values used elsewhere).
description: Once a scan is marked abandoned/timed_out/completed_with_warnings, the frontend's 15s fallback poll interval never recognizes it as finished and never calls clearInterval - it polls forever for the life of the component, the progress card silently freezes at its last %, and the user never sees a failure/abandoned toast. CONFIRMED: verified all 3 terminal-status arrays are missing all 3 values, and that scan-reconciler.job.js genuinely sets 'abandoned' in 5 code paths.
tags: verified-note: Yes - both cache-override and terminal-status-list gaps directly confirmed

title: Finding-to-control mapping is display-only, one-directional, with zero click-through in either surface
description:
`FindingComplianceControls.jsx:70-181` renders framework/requirement/title/description for a finding, but every cell is plain Text/Badge with no Link/href/onClick anywhere in the component - confirmed by full read. `ResourceFindingsPanel.jsx:580-591` does the same. There is no way to jump from a cloud-posture finding to the actual control record in /grc-framework. The reverse direction is also broken: `requirement-resource-resolver.service.js:384-412` builds the `resources[]` array consumed by the GRC control detail drawer - it enumerates evidence/policy/certification/integration/vendor/trust rows but never adds cloud-posture findings as individual rows. `FrameworkComplianceMap.jsx`'s TYPE_COLOR map (lines 606-611) and href router (lines 650-679) have branches for every resource type except 'cloud'. The control-list row only shows a bare aggregate number ('12 automated'), and opening the drawer shows the same resources table with no cloud entries at all.

Auditor-facing breakage: an auditor sampling 'why is control X covered?' sees '12 automated' with no way to see which 12 checks, which resources, pass or fail, or provider - and starting from a specific Prowler finding, there is no way to confirm which control it evidences without manually re-deriving the mapping.

component: /grc-framework coverage scoring for controls with cloud-posture evidence
title: A control can show 'Covered' while its cloud-posture evidence is 100% FAILing
description:
Both requirement- and control-level scoring weight 'cloud' as a small minority dimension out of 100 (`client-compliance-sync.service.js:1847-1850`: evidence 25/policy 15/cert 10/risk 10/vendor 10/trust 10/cloud 10/integration 10; control level :2653-2654: evidence 25/policy 15/risk 10/vendor 10/trust 10/cloud 15/integration 15), and `DEFAULT_COVERAGE_THRESHOLDS = {covered:70, partial:30}` (:128) marks anything >=70 'covered'. `onCloudPostureScanCompleted` (:1975-2004) sets `cloudScore = dominantStatus==='FAIL' ? 0 : ...` (line 1982) for a fully-failing control. Arithmetic: evidence+policy+cert+risk+vendor+trust already totals 80 (requirement level) or 70 (control level) with cloud=0 and integration=0 - either total already clears the 70-point 'covered' threshold with every single cloud check FAILing.

Auditor-facing breakage: this is the exact 'satisfied control, open failing finding' scenario an ISO 27001 auditor is trained to catch - the platform actively produces it by design, because cloud evidence is capped at 10-15% of a control's score with no override rule for a FAIL dominant status.
